title: Acceptance Criteria Authoring
body:
This record covers Acceptance Criteria Authoring within the End-to-End Task Acceptance Tests Database. Defines what must be true before a task counts as completed. The record is written as a complete, human-readable file: it states what the method is, when it applies, what it needs, what it produces, and where its limits lie.

How it works. Criterion method: completion requires every acceptance check to pass with captured evidence; a failed check blocks sign-off until remediated. In a simple case the method is applied to a single, well-defined item; in a compounded case several items are combined and their interactions are tracked; in the most complex case the full chain is carried end to end with checks at each stage.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record executes the worked calculation for this topic at build time, and its output is stored beside the code so any reader can compare the two. The numbers in the demo are ordinary working values for this topic, chosen so the arithmetic can be checked by hand as well as by running the program.
